page: Microsoft Azure E2as_v7 is an entry-level memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 family, provisioned through Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, allocating 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Advanced instruction sets are supported, including AVX-512 (foundation, VNNI, and BF16), AVX_VNNI, and cryptographic extensions such as VAES and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It does not include bundled local disk storage or GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a divergence between single-threaded compute and multi-threaded throughput. Driven by the 4.5 GHz clock frequency, the AMD EPYC core achieves top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng tests (3746.07) as well as compression operations, with single-threaded gzip throughput reaching 40.52 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 18.03 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the physical constraint of a single underlying core, with multi-core stress-ng (3755.57) and PassMark CPU (5089.01) ranking in lower tiers. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measured 43.28 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 33.7 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the mid-range bracket.

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-memory profile, the E2as_v7 provides high memory density at an entry resource footprint, though absolute throughput is limited by its dual-vCPU ceiling and reliance on network-attached storage. The hardware profile is optimal for low-concurrency, memory-heavy workloads. Common targets include small relational databases, Redis caching layers, single-threaded analytical tasks, and data staging pipelines requiring high per-thread memory capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure E2as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor running at 4.5 GHz. Deployed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 2 dedicated vCPUs originating from 1 physical core alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio with 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions, while excluding local storage and GPU hardware. Benchmarks show top-tier single-threaded computation and data compression rates, including 40.52 GB/sec in gzip compression and 3746.07 in single-core stress-ng tests. However, overall multi-core throughput and database transactions remain bounded by the single-core topology. The instance is targeted at memory-sensitive, low-concurrency workloads such as small in-memory caches, lightweight database servers, and single-threaded batch data transformations requiring large memory capacity.
